title: T-237 House / UNO MÁS UNO Arquitectos
text:
T-237 House / UNO MÁS UNO Arquitectos

Casa T-237 is conceived as a unique architectural piece with a rectangular geometry, resting on the southern boundary of the site and oriented toward a northern courtyard that organizes its relationship with the exterior. With an area of 1,290 sq ft (120 m²), the house proposes a precise response to the essential conditions of living, based on an elementary programmatic organization and a conscious exploration of the expressive and spatial possibilities of the material. The main volume, measuring 18 feet wide by 59 feet long (5.50 meters by 18 meters), concentrates the entirety of the domestic program on a single floor. The kitchen, dining room, living room, two bedrooms, and a bathroom are arranged in a succession of contiguous spaces open to the north. This organization establishes a constant relationship between the interior environments and the courtyard, favoring natural light and visual continuity while reducing formal complexity to a domestic-scale piece with a longitudinal configuration.

title: Mr. Belvedere House / Linework Architecture

Mr. Belvedere House / Linework Architecture

Located in Northeast Seattle, Mr. Belvedere is a substantial remodel and addition to an unassuming 1940s single-family ranch house with a focus on sustainability, durability, indoor-outdoor living and generational flexibility.

title: Campus du Parc / IT'S Studio
text:
Campus du Parc / IT'S Studio

For twenty years, the former Nanterre School of Architecture was a ghost building, yet its spatial power never faded. Designed in 1971 by Jacques Kalisz and Roger Salem, it was the first public building of a vast social redevelopment project. It stands in the heart of the André-Malraux Park, conceived from the beginning as a true cultural city, surrounded by public buildings dedicated to culture such as the Théâtre Nanterre-Amandiers and the Paris Opera Ballet School. Abandoned since 2004, the site entered the Inventons la Métropole du Grand Paris 2 competition in 2018. The Campus du Parc project was born, curated by IT'S, in a shared path with Eiffage Immobilier, developer of the operation, and the De Vinci Higher Education group, which opened its new campus headquarters for 4,500 engineering, business, and digital students.

title: Impermanence by Design: An Architectural History of Antarctica
text:
Impermanence by Design: An Architectural History of Antarctica

"Antarctica is known through narratives," states Victoria Nuviala Antelo during the lecture on Inhabiting the Extreme: An Architectural Biography of Antarctica, presented at the Buenos Aires International Architecture Biennial. Indeed, throughout architectural history, numerous stories, experiences, ways of inhabiting, and building practices have often been excluded from official narratives. Buried beneath thick layers of ice, the history of Antarctic architecture tells a story of impermanence. The ice surrounding the continent expands and contracts each year, doubling its surface area, while the species that inhabit it migrate and return according to their life cycles. Ice covers structures as katabatic winds erase the traces of more than 200 years of human presence. Explorations, settlements, architectural interventions, and ways of inhabiting remain concealed within one of the most extreme landscapes on the planet.

title: YUKI Office / UENOA
text:
YUKI Office / UENOA

YUKI office is the headquarters of a company in Kuki, Saitama, that sells organic vegetables under the philosophy of "thinking about food and health." The client asked for a building that would immediately convey the company's mission to anyone who visits: to deliver safe, trustworthy produce to consumers and to help preserve Japan's traditional food culture. After the Great East Japan Earthquake, the company used its own distribution network to support the affected areas, and it wanted a headquarters that could also support the local community in future disasters.

title: Creative Rebellion: Design, Knowledge and Experimentation at interihotel MAD26
text:
Creative Rebellion: Design, Knowledge and Experimentation at interihotel MAD26

From November 17 to 19, 2026, interihotel MAD26 will bring together architects, interior designers, hospitality operators, and specialized brands at IFEMA Madrid. Organized by AMBIT Living Spaces Cluster, the event is expected to welcome more than 14,000 professionals, 350 exhibiting brands, and over 200 international speakers. Under the theme Creative Rebellion, it will combine talks, workshops, five specialized forums, and full-scale experimental spaces to explore new approaches to hotel and restaurant design.

title: What Accumulates? Lessons on Materiality, Memory, and Public Space from Amman Design Week 2026
text:
What Accumulates? Lessons on Materiality, Memory, and Public Space from Amman Design Week 2026

After a seven-year pause, Amman Design Week returned to Jordan with a premise that feels closely tied to the city itself: that nothing is ever entirely new. Under the theme "Accumulations," the fourth edition of the biennial event brought together more than 220 designers, makers, architects, and collectives across exhibitions, public interventions, talks, workshops, and performances from October 2 to 17. The premise was particularly relevant to Amman, a city whose architecture has been shaped by waves of construction, migration, adaptation, and reuse, where accumulation is not simply a metaphor.

text:
Circular Town Hall Krimpenerwaard / Ector Hoogstad Architecten

Following the merger that established the municipality of Krimpenerwaard, the local government sought to unite its organization in one central town hall: a welcoming, accessible place for residents and entrepreneurs, a collaborative workplace, and an affordable building that would advance circular construction.

title: The XIV Ibero-American Biennial Comes to Brasília Under the Theme “Caring for Life”
text:
The XIV Ibero-American Biennial Comes to Brasília Under the Theme “Caring for Life”

The Bienal Iberoamericana de Arquitectura y Urbanismo (Ibero-American Biennial of Architecture and Urbanism), known as BIAU for its Spanish name, is an international event promoted by the Government of Spain through its Ministry of Housing and Urban Agenda (MIVAU) since 1998. Held every two years in a different location across Latin America and the Iberian Peninsula, it recognizes, awards, and disseminates high-quality works that reflect the diversity of Ibero-American architecture and urbanism. Following its thirteenth edition, "CLIMAS: Acciones para el buen vivir" (CLIMATES: Actions for Good Living), held in Lima, Peru, in 2024, the XIV BIAU will take place in Brasília from November 3 to 6, 2026, under the theme "Cuidar la Vida" (Caring for Life). This edition structures its reflection around four themes: water, vegetation, housing, and communities, exploring the relationship between architecture and the environmental, social, and cultural conditions that sustain life.

title: From Hiding to Civic Presence: How Wastewater Plants Entered the City
text:
From Hiding to Civic Presence: How Wastewater Plants Entered the City

When London's main drainage was completed north of the Thames in 1868, the Metropolitan Board of Works marked the occasion with a banquet held inside a sewage pumping station. Abbey Mills had been built over the previous three years by the engineer Joseph Bazalgette, working with the architect Charles Driver, laid out on a cruciform plan with eight beam engines, two on each arm. Its style has been read as Byzantine, Italian Medieval, Russian, Ruskinian Gothic and Moorish, and its twin ventilation chimneys, richly ornamented, rose more than sixty meters. The builder called it an elegant structure in a swamp and thought it might pass for a mosque or a temple.

title: Monastic Field House / ROOMOOR
text:
Monastic Field House / ROOMOOR

Around 2005, a devout family donated a parcel of land on the highway near Surat at Baleshwar for the construction of a Jain temple and its ancillary structures such as dharamshalas (accommodation), bhojanshala (community kitchen and dining hall), and vyakhyan kendra (spiritual discourse hall). As a token of appreciation, the presiding head monk promised the family a small private lot within the precinct. The family chose to build a house twenty years later.

title: Companion Villa / AsNow Design & Construct
text:
Companion Villa / AsNow Design & Construct

Companion Villa is a residential project that responds to the challenges of density, scale, and neighborhood context while maintaining a minimalist modernist language.

title: Piedra Bay House / DE SPACE
text:
Piedra Bay House / DE SPACE

At Casa Piedra Bay, the landscape is not simply contemplated; it becomes an essential part of the experience of inhabiting the house. Located in Palmar de Ocoa, Azua, Dominican Republic, the project emerges from an arid coastal setting defined by the contrast between the mountains and the Caribbean Sea. The architecture responds to this environment through a spatial composition that prioritizes natural ventilation, filtered sunlight, privacy, and a continuous connection with the surrounding landscape.

title: M38 House / Muda Prefab
text:
M38 House / Muda Prefab

The M38 House is born from a question: how can we industrialize construction without standardizing architecture? This 38 m² prefabricated house aligns domestic space design with manufacturing, transportation, and assembly processes. Its first unit is installed inside the workshop where it was built, serving as a showroom that allows visitors to experience the spaces and learn about the house's materials within its manufacturing context.

title: Espiga House / Grupo Primitivo
text:
Espiga House / Grupo Primitivo

Vivienda Espiga explores the potential of the structure as an organizing and qualifying element of architectural space, transcending its role as mere support to become the primary articulator of the living experience. Through a sequence of timber structural frames, the project establishes an order that defines pathways, articulates rooms, and builds a material identity where structure, architecture, and landscape integrate into a single expression.

title: MUZEU – Thought and Contemporary Art / Carvalho Araújo
text:
MUZEU – Thought and Contemporary Art / Carvalho Araújo

MUZEU transforms the former Judicial Court of Braga into a new space dedicated to contemporary art and thought. The project preserves the existing facades and integrates the 14th-century medieval wall, reorganizing the interior through a new contemporary structure.

title: Courtyard House / Hennessey Architecture
text:
Courtyard House / Hennessey Architecture

For this modestly-scaled renovation of a classic suburban Mill Valley house, the home was thought not only as a shelter, but also as a bridge: from past to present; from one landscape condition to another; and from what a family wanted to what they could have. Designed for a couple with two young children, the house is meant to support their current needs as a young family and grow with them.

title: Cabin Budor / R21 Arkitekter
text:
Cabin Budor / R21 Arkitekter

The commission consists of the design and construction of a weekend cabin in Budor. The main challenge is to integrate the volume into the landscape through its materiality, seeking to ensure that the project interferes as little as possible with the natural surroundings. The architecture aims to establish a dialogue with the landscape without attempting to dominate it.

title: Wood Innovation Summit: Innovation in Industrialized Timber, Architecture, and Construction
text:
Wood Innovation Summit: Innovation in Industrialized Timber, Architecture, and Construction

The first edition of the Wood Innovation Summit in Chile will take place on October 27, bringing together architects and industry stakeholders for an international gathering to reflect on innovation in timber and its role in the future of design and construction.

The event will feature special guests Lina Ghotmeh and Sauerbruch Hutton, alongside architects Nicolás Urzúa, Tomás Villalón, Cristián Izquierdo, and 57 Studio. Through their diverse perspectives and professional experiences, the summit aims to foster dialogue around the possibilities of timber as a material for contemporary architecture.

title: “Architecture Must Return to Its Essence”: Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu on the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale
text:
“Architecture Must Return to Its Essence”: Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu on the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale

"Architecture must return to its essence." With this statement, Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu establish the central premise of their curatorial vision for the 20th International Architecture Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia, taking place from May 8 to November 21, 2027, across the Giardini, the Arsenale, and throughout Venice. Titled "Do Architecture – For the Possibility of Coexistence Facing a Real Reality", the exhibition calls for a return to the physical act of making architecture, at a time when, according to the curators, the discipline has become increasingly disconnected from lived reality through excessive abstraction, commercialization, and digitalization.

title: Inherited Ground: Designing Houses on Contaminated Land
text:
Inherited Ground: Designing Houses on Contaminated Land

Industrial activity can end long before its effects disappear from the land. Factories close, buildings are demolished, and former industrial districts gradually become part of new residential developments. Yet the soil beneath them may still contain traces of their previous use, sometimes requiring extensive intervention before construction can begin.

title: Palais de Justice de Lille / OMA
text:
Palais de Justice de Lille / OMA

Any new architectural addition to the city of Lille has to address the past, the present and the future. That is even more true on the site of Vauban's former fortifications – used in Lille as a zone where modernity can be organized without damaging the city.

title: How Much Information Does a BIM Model Really Need?
text:
How Much Information Does a BIM Model Really Need?

Building Information Modeling has made it possible to attach an enormous amount of information to each element of a design. A wall can carry its fire resistance class and its cost group, and later even the maintenance information a facility manager will need. That possibility creates a temptation: if the model can hold more data, it should. In the process, an important question of efficiency can get lost: does the project actually need this information, and does it need it now?
